add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.texto: readSequence accepts a child whose encoded size exceeds the remaining declared sequence length instead of rejecting the malformed DER. For example, `30 05 02 01 01 02 01 01` produces two integers and is accepted by asn1derToConcatenatedRS even though the second integer extends beyond the sequence boundary, silently converting an invalid signature encoding. Reject a child larger than the remaining sequence payload and require the sequence length to be consumed exactly.

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.texto: Updating match_count inside validation counts a single blocked signup twice. UsersController#create calls user.valid? at line 168 and then user.save at line 172, and both run EmailValidator and should_block?, inflating the advertised blocked-attempt statistics. Record the attempt once at the signup boundary rather than as a side effect of each model validation.

The match counter uses an unlocked read-modify-save operation. Two concurrent attempts can load the same match_count and both save the same incremented value, losing one match from the statistics. Update the counter atomically in SQL together with last_match_at, or lock the row around the read and write.

The blocking lookup compares the raw email string without normalizing domain capitalization. User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] unchanged, so an address blocked as bad@example.com can sign up as bad@EXAMPLE.COM even though it routes to the same mailbox. Normalize email domains consistently when storing blocked addresses and when looking them up, using the existing Email.downcase behavior.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.texto: canManage() accepts the VIEW scope for all groups, granting write authorization to a read-only administrator. Inherited requireManage() uses this result in GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup, allowing that administrator to create groups or move existing groups to the top level. Require only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE here.

The new Groups resource creation path never assigns the Groups type to the authorization resource created by getOrCreateResource. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission enumerates resources using findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE), so per-group permissions created through this path are excluded and group-based user counts cannot find their permitted groups. Assign the appropriate resource type when creating the group authorization resource.

The enumeration passes and returns the authorization resource ID instead of the group model ID stored in the resource name. hasPermission resolves its argument with resourceStore.findByName, while user queries compare the returned IDs against group membership IDs, so enumerated resources are evaluated against the wrong target and cannot select their group members. Use groupResource.getName() for both the permission lookup and the granted group ID.

The new V2 group-ID result is consumed by a JPA filtering implementation that still requires a legacy authorization resource named group.resource.<groupId>. UsersResource passes this result into JpaUserProvider search/count paths, whose groupsWithPermissionsSubquery checks for that legacy name, whereas the new schema creates resources named only by group ID; therefore V2-only group permissions cannot return or count their members even with correct group IDs. Update the JPA filtering contract to support V2 resource naming rather than requiring a V1 resource.

advanced-date-override-handling-and-time.texto: A matching date override returns true before the busy-calendar checks run. Both fixed and rotating hosts pass their busy intervals into this function, so an existing booking or calendar conflict inside an override is now advertised as available. Continue to the busy checks after validating override availability instead of returning true.

The override bounds check only rejects disjoint slots rather than requiring the entire event to fit inside the override. For a 10:00–11:00 override, a 09:30–10:30 or 10:30–11:30 event passes, and a slot starting exactly at 11:00 also passes. Require slotStartTime >= override start and slotEndTime <= override end.

The override search rejects a slot when any override on the date is disjoint from it, even if another override contains it. With overrides 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected against the afternoon interval and a 15:00 slot against the morning interval. Group the date's overrides and accept availability when any interval contains the complete slot.

The recurring-hours check rejects availability if any interval on the weekday excludes the slot, instead of checking whether an interval includes it. A normal split schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00 consequently loses all slots, since each slot is outside one interval. Require a containing interval on the weekday and reject when none exists; this also handles fixed hosts with no hours on that weekday.

The working-hours end value is calculated from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime. A fixed host ending work at 17:00 therefore passes a 16:30–17:30 event generated from a rotating host's longer availability. Compare the actual event end against the working-hours end.

Converting override boundaries to hour/minute values discards date rollover introduced by the timezone offset. A UTC override from 20:00–22:00 viewed in UTC+3 becomes startTime 1380 and endTime 60, so the formerly valid interval becomes inverted and produces no slots instead of availability spanning 23:00–01:00. Preserve the converted dates and split intervals crossing invitee midnight into their respective days.

advanced-query-processing-architecture-g.texto: Early interpolation is followed by another applyTemplateVariables call in DataSourceWithBackend.query, so substituted values are interpreted as template syntax again. For example, a variable value or literal ad hoc filter value containing `$other` is inserted here and then replaced with the dashboard's other variable on execution, changing the requested LogQL match; shard splitting adds yet another interpolation pass through runSplitQuery. Ensure outgoing split requests bypass further template substitution after preparation, and test through the real runQuery/backend preparation path rather than mocking runQuery.

async-import-of-the-appstore-packages-ca.texto: The async forEach callback turns getCalendar failures into ignored rejected promises that the surrounding try/catch cannot catch. For example, an Exchange credential that fails decryption or JSON parsing now produces an unhandled rejection instead of reaching the existing logger, potentially terminating the process; the same regression is present in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts. Replace forEach with an awaited loop or await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) inside the try block.

authzservice-improve-authz-caching-grafa.texto: The denial-cache key does not distinguish underscores inside the resource name from the separator before the parent folder. For the same namespace, user and action, a denial for Name="a_b", ParentFolder="c" also denies Name="a", ParentFolder="b_c", even when the latter resource is authorized, because Check returns before evaluating permissions on a cache hit. Encode the fields unambiguously, for example by serializing the key tuple or length-prefixing each component.

comprehensive-workflow-reminder-manageme.texto: The default cancellation path only marks the reminder as cancelled, even when its scheduled send is less than ten minutes away. Booking cancellation and reschedule-request callers use this path, so they no longer attempt immediate provider cancellation, and the cron cannot reliably cancel the send because SendGrid requires cancellations more than ten minutes before delivery; a cron run after delivery also deletes the row before processing cancellations. Cancel at the provider immediately when handling near-term reminders rather than relying exclusively on deferred processing.

Successful cancellation rows are not deleted until every SendGrid request in the loop succeeds, and one rejection exits the entire loop. If a later request fails, earlier successfully cancelled batches remain in the database; the next run POSTs cancellation again for those batches, which SendGrid rejects with 400 for an already-cancelled batch, preventing later reminders from being cancelled before delivery. Handle errors per reminder and persist each successful cancellation's deletion before proceeding to the next reminder, treating an already-cancelled provider status idempotently.

database-performance-optimizations-grafa.texto: The SQLite fallback rebuilds the entire accumulated ID list with fmt.Sprintf for every ID, making SQL construction quadratic in the batch size. Large batches explicitly supported by this PR, including the 32767-row configuration in the new test, repeatedly allocate and copy growing strings for both annotation and orphan-tag cleanup, adding substantial CPU and allocation overhead before any DELETE executes. Build the list with strings.Builder and append each formatted ID once instead.

The ticker change runs the entire cleanup service every minute instead of every ten minutes, rather than changing only annotation cleanup. Each tick invokes all eight jobs in clean, increasing recurring database and filesystem cleanup work tenfold; when a cleanup takes more than a minute, a pending tick also starts the next cycle immediately, eliminating the previous idle interval. Preserve the ten-minute interval for this query-splitting change.

enhanced-pagination-performance-for-high.texto: The unconditional administrator check dereferences organization_context.member even though organization-token requests can have no membership. OrganizationAuditPermission permits organization-scoped authentication through from_rpc_auth, but these requests now raise AttributeError even without optimized_pagination=true, breaking previously working audit-log access. Evaluate this check only when optimization is requested and guard member against None.

OptimizedCursorPaginator treats its ordering key as numeric, but its audit-log caller sets order_by='-datetime'. Nonempty pages pass datetime objects to math.floor/math.ceil while building cursors and raise TypeError; subsequent timestamp cursors also lack the datetime conversion required by the database predicate. Inherit DateTimePaginator or preserve its get_item_key and value_from_cursor conversions.

The new advanced negative-offset branch passes a negative slice bound directly to a Django QuerySet, which explicitly rejects negative indexing. An optimized request with a cursor such as '0:-1:0' raises an uncaught slicing exception instead of performing the advertised reverse pagination. Reject negative offsets with a pagination validation error or implement reverse traversal using reversed ordering and nonnegative bounds.

feat-add-calendar-cache-status-and-actio.texto: Successful cache deletion does not invalidate viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and relies exclusively on an optional onSuccess callback. EventAdvancedTab renders the wrapper without onChanged, so its cached response continues to show the old cache timestamp and delete action after the underlying rows have been deleted. Invalidate connectedCalendars on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

Passing an empty update object to updateManyByCredentialId does not refresh Prisma's @updatedAt field. The new operation therefore leaves SelectedCalendar.updatedAt unchanged after cache population instead of recording the update as intended. Pass { updatedAt: new Date() } explicitly.

The environment update uses BSD sed syntax (`sed -i ''`), which fails with GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, the script leaves the old URL in place but still reports success, so webhook testing continues targeting the previous tunnel. Use a portable temporary-file replacement or choose the appropriate in-place syntax for the host platform, and check the command's exit status.

feat-upsampling-support-upsampled-error-.texto: Replacing count() with 'upsampled_count() as count' breaks responses requested with transformAliasToInputFormat=1. BaseQueryBuilder.process_results translates the count alias to 'upsampled_count() as count', but organization_events.py still serializes the original count() key, so the serializer's r.get(column, 0) returns zero for populated buckets. Preserve the original public count() name when translating the rewritten query results.

The top-N path upsamples only the timeseries columns while leaving the selected fields and ranking aggregation as raw count(). discover.top_events_timeseries first selects the top groups using selected_columns and orderby, so a group with fewer stored events but a larger sample-weight total is excluded in favor of a lower weighted-count group. Apply the weighted count transformation consistently to the top-group selection and ranking as well as the timeseries query, preserving their public aliases.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.texto: Each new strategy reuses the factory-owned queue_pool even though the previous strategy's close() permanently shuts down that pool and its workers. Arroyo closes and recreates strategies on partition changes, so after the first rebalance subsequent submissions target stopped queues and are caught as submission errors and marked complete, allowing unprocessed results to be committed. Create a fresh pool for each strategy assignment instead of reusing a pool shut down by the previous strategy.

Graceful close/join stops the commit thread before draining work, and pool.shutdown sets worker exit flags before queued items have been processed. Closing while results are queued therefore abandons queued items, while results completed after the commit thread exits never receive a final commit and are replayed on reassignment; join() does not drain them because it only calls close() again. Let close stop intake, then have join drain queued and in-flight work, commit the final completed offsets, and only then stop workers and the commit loop, respecting the supplied timeout.

The worker queues have no capacity limit, and strategy.submit always accepts additional Kafka messages without signaling backpressure. When a worker is slow or incoming throughput exceeds processing capacity, queued WorkItems retain decoded results and original messages indefinitely while offset sets also grow, exhausting consumer memory instead of leaving the backlog in Kafka. Bound total pending work and raise Arroyo MessageRejected before accepting a message when capacity is exhausted; ensure the broad submit exception handler does not swallow that rejection.

feature-per-topic-unsubscribe-option-in-.texto: The unsubscribe action dereferences TopicUser.find_by without handling a missing record. A logged-in user opening this URL for a visible topic with no topic_users row receives a NoMethodError instead of being unsubscribed; TopicView does not create that row. Handle the missing record and persist the chosen level through TopicUser.change, which supports creating it.

Saving the notification level directly omits notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at that TopicUser.change sets for explicit preference changes. For rows with a null reason, update_last_read can promote the topic back to tracking and TrackedTopicsUpdater can overwrite even the muted level, undoing the unsubscribe choice. Persist the level through TopicUser.change as set_notifications does.

These GET routes mutate the authenticated visitor's notification preferences without a CSRF-protected submission. An attacker can link or redirect a logged-in user to a known topic's unsubscribe URL and silently downgrade or mute that user's subscription, since the action also skips check_xhr. Make GET display a confirmation and perform the mutation with a CSRF-protected POST or PUT.

The client-side unsubscribe route only calls PostStream.loadTopicView, which fetches the ordinary topic JSON endpoint rather than invoking the unsubscribe action. A client-side transition to this route displays the unsubscribe confirmation while leaving the notification level unchanged; only a full server request currently changes it. Have the route perform the preference-changing request before showing success, or require an explicit submission on this page.

implement-recovery-key-support-for-user-.texto: Successful creation in external storage leaves any existing locally stored recovery-code credential active. If a user already has local recovery codes before their storage provider gains recovery-code support, regeneration now skips RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential's deletion of the old set; UserCredentialManager.isValid falls back to the local validator when external validation fails, so old codes still authenticate after replacement. Remove the existing local recovery-code credential when the external update succeeds.

The new recovery-code validator returns success without consuming the matching code in the test storage. Every subsequent login can reuse the same code, and getCredentials reconstructs the original full list, so the displayed code number and remaining-code count never advance and exhaustion never triggers regeneration. Persist removal of the consumed code and expose the updated credential state; extend the integration test to reject replay and verify progression to the next code.

optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.texto: The new ZADD writes sorted sets into the same span-buf:s namespace that existing consumers populated with Redis sets. During deployment, processing a trace with an existing buffer raises WRONGTYPE, and the new ZSCAN reader also cannot flush those existing buffers, preventing successful batch processing until the old keys expire. Version the buffer namespace and coordinate queue references, or provide an explicit migration/draining transition before switching Redis types.

ZUNIONSTORE defaults to SUM, so merging buffers adds end timestamps when the same payload exists in both inputs. Replaying a child batch after its parent has been redirected recreates the temporary parent buffer while the canonical buffer already contains that payload; the merge doubles its score and incorrectly protects old spans from eviction over newer spans. Specify AGGREGATE MAX (also on the parent-buffer merge) to preserve timestamp scores for duplicate payloads.

scale-color-lightness-must-use-secondary.texto: The light-theme branch changes the topic-summary heading from 20% lightness scaling to 50%, reducing the default foreground from approximately #4e4e4e to #919191. This normal-weight, 1em heading now has only about 3.2:1 contrast against the default white background, below the 4.5:1 requirement for normal text and making the summary heading harder to read in existing light themes. Preserve the original 20% light-theme argument and use 80% for the complementary dark-theme argument, as the corresponding desktop heading does.

ux-show-complete-url-path-if-website-dom.texto: The new website_name attribute bypasses the visibility restriction applied to website by UserSerializer.untrusted_attributes. An anonymous viewer of a TL0 user's profile now receives the restricted website's host (and path for matching domains), and the updated template displays it even though website itself is omitted. Add website_name to untrusted_attributes so it uses the same restrict_user_fields? guard as website.

add-caching-support-for-identityprovider.texto: The early return compares an organization-aware original model against the updated model, so a disabled organization makes an otherwise login-eligible original fail getLoginPredicate(). After warming a public organization's login cache, disabling the organization and setting its IDP to hide-on-login or link-only makes both predicates false and skips invalidation; re-enabling the organization then displays that IDP from the stale cache because the login bean only rechecks isEnabled(). Compare persisted IDP eligibility independently of organization enabled state, for example by loading the original through idpDelegate.getById(), before deciding whether to invalidate.

The cold-cache load discards the fully loaded delegate models and retains only their IDs, then calls getById separately for every result. When individual IDP caches are cold, getById delegates to JPA for each ID, turning the existing bulk login lookup into a bulk lookup plus N individual database loads on the login request. Retain the loaded models and populate the individual caches from them, or return the loaded organization-aware models for this miss while caching the result IDs.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.texto: The global canView() grant bypasses evaluation of explicit permissions on the requested client. With an all-clients VIEW grant and a per-client denial, this branch authorizes the denied client; ClientsResource.getClients() also uses the global result to bypass all per-client checks. Evaluate the concrete client resource before falling back to the all-clients resource, and do not expose a global listing shortcut when individual denials must be honored.

The Clients type lookup selects the synthetic all-clients resource rather than the individual client resources created by getOrCreateResource(), which does not set their type. Consequently, individual grants are omitted and an all-clients grant can return the literal name "Clients" as a client ID; AvailableRoleMappingResource.getRoleIdsWithPermissions() dereferences realm.getClientById(cid) on these results. Ensure individual client resources carry the matching type and expand the synthetic all-clients grant into real client IDs instead of returning its name.

canView() does not recognize an all-clients MANAGE grant even though canView(client) treats MANAGE as sufficient to view each client. ClientsResource.getClients() therefore loads the unpaginated client stream and performs per-client authorization and access evaluations before applying pagination for these administrators, making a paginated request scan the realm's clients. Include the implied MANAGE visibility in the listing authorization design while preserving explicit per-client denials.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.texto: The team-admin-or-owner check requires both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, rejecting ADMIN members who are neither the organizer nor an attendee. isTeamAdmin already accepts ADMIN and OWNER, while isTeamOwner accepts only OWNER, so ordinary team administrators receive FORBIDDEN when adding guests. Use isTeamAdmin alone, or combine the checks with OR.

uniqueGuests does not deduplicate addresses within the submitted guests array. A direct API request containing the same new email twice passes the server schema and inserts duplicate Attendee rows, resulting in duplicate invitations and attendee entries; the database has no booking/email unique constraint. Deduplicate the submitted addresses server-side before filtering and inserting them.

The blacklist check compares unnormalized guest addresses with lowercased blacklist entries. An authorized attendee can invite a blocked address by changing its case or using a plus-address alias, bypassing the base-email normalization enforced by handleNewBooking. Normalize each guest with extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase() before comparing it against the blacklist.

add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.texto:
The common-suffix scan can overlap the already matched prefix, producing invalid substring bounds when constructing the validation message. For example, '

' sanitizes to '

', giving start=3 and end=1, so value.substring(3, 2) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and aborts theme verification instead of reporting illegal HTML. Limit the suffix scan to the unmatched lengths after start in both strings.

The account-console validation message now uses Java MessageFormat placeholders and ChoiceFormat syntax instead of i18next interpolation. account-ui/src/i18n.ts loads these strings unchanged into plain i18next, and ui-shared/src/user-profile/utils.ts supplies numeric interpolation parameters, so users see literal '{0}', '{1}', '{2}' and the choice expression in multivalued validation errors. Retain i18next-compatible placeholders and implement pluralization using its supported message format rather than Java ChoiceFormat.

The Lithuanian OTP setup instruction has been replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare'). login-config-totp.ftl renders this resource directly, so Lithuanian users receive an Italian setup instruction; the same erroneous replacement appears in the Lithuanian account bundle. Replace these values with Lithuanian instructions while retaining the removal of embedded links.

anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.texto: A device rejected by the limit is accepted on its next request because tagDeviceUI caches the device ID before CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Repeating the same request hits that cache and returns success, allowing anonymous authentication for devices beyond the configured limit for 29 minutes. Cache only successfully persisted devices and ensure cached entries represent successful admission.

Limit enforcement is skipped entirely when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent because TagDevice returns nil immediately for an empty device ID. An unauthenticated caller can omit this client-controlled header and obtain an anonymous identity even when the device limit is full. When a positive limit is configured, require a valid device identity before admitting anonymous requests.

The device-count check and subsequent insert are not atomic. Concurrent requests with distinct new device IDs can both observe a count below the limit and both insert, exceeding the configured cap; the unique device_id constraint cannot prevent this. Serialize admission with a database-level lock or equivalent atomic mechanism that works across Grafana instances.

dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex.texto: The asynchronous legacy write derives its timeout context from the HTTP request context, which is canceled when the handler returns. Consequently, successful unified writes can have their backup writes canceled immediately rather than receiving the intended ten seconds; the same issue affects Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection. Derive the background timeout from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) to retain request values without inheriting request-end cancellation.

Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo rather than an updateWrapper containing the object committed to unified storage. Playlist legacyStorage.Update invokes objInfo.UpdatedObject against its own old object, so a patch is recomputed against potentially stale legacy data and can produce a different result or fail even after the unified update succeeds. Pass an updateWrapper with upstream: objInfo and updated: res to the legacy update.

The successful Delete metric passes the object name into the histogram's kind label. Each distinct deleted resource name therefore creates a permanently retained histogram series in the global HistogramVec, increasing application memory and scrape cardinality with historical deletions rather than resource kinds. Pass options.Kind instead of name.

The unified-storage Create failure is recorded with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration; the Update failure branch at line 129 has the same inversion, and the legacy DeleteCollection completion at line 166 incorrectly uses recordStorageDuration. Because these helpers observe separate backend histograms, unified failures disappear from unified error metrics and legacy collection-write outcomes pollute unified metrics, giving incorrect backend health and latency results. Use recordStorageDuration for the Create/Update storage failures and recordLegacyDuration for the asynchronous legacy DeleteCollection result.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.texto: The conditional is closed with `end if` rather than `end`, leaving an incomplete Ruby modifier-if in the generated ERB code. Rendering an existing embedded discussion therefore fails with a template syntax error. Replace this tag with `<%- end %>`.

The importer unconditionally calls `scrub` on `i.content`, although simple-rss exposes RSS description and content:encoded separately as `description` and `content_encoded`. A normal RSS entry containing those fields but no Atom-style content produces nil here and aborts the entire feed import. Select the available body across content_encoded, content, summary and description before processing it.

Feed contents are stored with the raw_html cook method without HTML sanitization. PollFeed passes external HTML directly into this method, absolutize_urls preserves script tags and event-handler attributes, and Post.cook returns that HTML unchanged, allowing a malicious feed entry to execute JavaScript on the forum origin when its post is viewed. Sanitize imported HTML with an explicit safe tag, attribute and URL-scheme policy before storing it as raw_html.

Every uncached embed URL invokes a complete feed download and import before attempting its own HTTP retrieval. The Redis throttle is keyed by the individual embed URL, so concurrent visitors to different new articles each download the same feed and iterate all its entries, multiplying network traffic and database lookups by articles times feed entries. Coalesce or throttle feed polling with a feed-scoped key rather than invoking a full poll independently for every missing article.

absolutize_urls resolves protocol-relative URLs against the article host and leaves document-relative URLs unchanged. For example, an image source of //cdn.example.com/image.png becomes http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.png, while images/photo.png resolves against the Discourse page instead of the original article, breaking imported images and links. Resolve href and src against the full article URL using URI.join rather than concatenating the origin.

feat-2fa-backup-codes-cal-com.texto: The backup-code branch accepts requests containing a nonempty totpCode without verifying either the password or that TOTP. The existing password checks at lines 113–125 are skipped when totpCode is supplied, so an attacker possessing a backup code can submit an arbitrary totpCode and log into a CAL account without its password. Require password verification for CAL backup-code authentication independently of whether totpCode is present.

Backup-code consumption overwrites the encrypted array using an unconditional update after reading and validating an earlier snapshot. Concurrent requests can both authenticate with the same one-time code; requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's removals and restore a consumed code. Use an atomic compare-and-swap against the previously read backupCodes value and accept authentication only if that conditional update succeeds, or serialize consumption with a database row lock.

feat-ecosystem-implement-cross-system-is.texto: The source check suppresses updates to every linked issue on the originating integration, not just the issue that emitted the webhook. A group can have multiple distinct external issue links on the same Jira integration (GroupLink is unique by group, linked_type and linked_id), so changing the assignee on one issue now leaves the other linked issues unchanged even when outbound assignment sync is enabled. Carry the originating external issue identity in AssignmentSource and skip only the matching outbound destination.

The queued default evaluates timezone.now() once when the module is imported rather than when an AssignmentSource is created. Every subsequent webhook handled by that process therefore receives the same queued timestamp, and to_dict exports an incorrect creation time. Use dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now) to generate the timestamp per instance.

feat-workflow-engine-add-in-hook-for-pro.texto: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits four abstract members from StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing them. MetricAlertFire still registers this class, so accessing detector.detector_handler for a metric_alert_fire detector raises TypeError at the constructor call in models/detector.py:86 and aborts process_detectors instead of returning the previous empty evaluation. Implement the required stateful methods before registering this subclass, or retain a concrete DetectorHandler implementation returning an empty dictionary until metric-alert evaluation is implemented.

feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.texto: The second `self.downsize` definition replaces the existing width/height version rather than overloading it in Ruby. `Jobs::ResizeEmoji#execute` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, which now raises ArgumentError instead of resizing uploaded emoji. Use a single method that supports both argument shapes, or give the geometry-string entry point a distinct name.

The fixed 10 MB limit is applied to attachments as well as images, replacing `max_attachment_size_kb` for attachment validation. Sites configured to accept attachments larger than 10 MB now have those valid uploads rejected in the browser even though UploadValidator still accepts them. Apply the fixed pre-resize limit only to images and retain the configured attachment limit for attachments.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.texto: The category query dereferences its first row before checking whether any row was returned. Sites without an explicit embed_category setting, or whose setting no longer matches a category name, fail the migration before reaching the uncategorized fallback. Read the first row safely and fall back when it is absent.

Legacy host values are inserted unchanged, bypassing the new model's scheme and path normalization. Existing values such as https://example.com/1234 consequently never match record_for_host's comparison against example.com, disabling embedding after upgrade. Normalize migrated values to the same representation used by the model before inserting them.

record_for_host compares URI.host, which excludes the port, against stored host strings that explicitly allow ports. A valid configured entry such as example.com:8080 therefore never authorizes http://example.com:8080 or supplies its category to imported topics. Use a consistent port representation when storing and matching hosts.

The save success callback replaces the server-returned category using categoryId even when categoryId is null. Saving a new host without selecting a category makes the server assign uncategorized, but the callback clears its category in the client and displays an empty category until reload. Preserve the category from the response or resolve the returned category_id rather than the submitted null value.

feature-localization-fallbacks-server-si.texto: The new fallback result depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator caches no-argument translations using only key, config.locale, and backend.object_id. A translation resolved through one site's default locale is therefore reused for the same user locale on another site sharing the backend, and changing the site's default locale can also leave the previous fallback text cached. Include the site and fallback configuration in the translation cache key, or invalidate/partition the cache when that context changes.

Fallback locales are loaded only through the new controller callback, leaving background translations without their fallback data. Jobs::Base sets I18n.locale and executes jobs directly, while the accelerator loads only config.locale; the fallback backend then looks up English directly without loading its YAML files, so a missing localized key in a fresh worker produces a missing translation instead of English. Ensure the fallback chain is loaded at the translation boundary as well, so non-controller callers receive the same fallback behavior.

fix-concurrent-group-access-to-prevent-n.texto: The test asserts caughtExceptions without waiting for the reader thread to finish. A read already in progress can fail and append its exception after the assertion, allowing this concurrency regression test to pass despite the server error it is intended to detect. Keep the worker reference and join it after signaling termination, before inspecting caughtExceptions.

The reader's stop flag is set only after every deletion succeeds, with no finally cleanup. If any remove() throws, the test exits while its non-daemon worker continues issuing group-list requests indefinitely, interfering with later tests and potentially preventing JVM shutdown. Place the stop signal and worker termination in a finally block around deletion.

fix-handle-collective-multiple-host-on-d.texto: The Google Meet fallback dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar when the destination list is empty or null. A booking using Google Meet without a destination calendar now throws before reaching the intended Cal Video fallback. Use mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration in the condition.

Video booking references now discard result.credentialId because it is only retained for calendar results. createMeeting returns the selected credential ID, and handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when the video reference has that ID, so newly created video meetings are left behind on cancellation. Preserve result.credentialId for video results too.

Office365 createEvent always selects the first host's destination even when EventManager invokes it with another host's credential. Collective bookings therefore POST to the organizer's calendar ID using the co-host's token instead of creating the co-host's event, causing calendar creation to fail. Accept the credentialId passed by CalendarManager and select the destination matching that credential.

The fallback searches for a calendar whose externalId equals the missing externalCalendarId, so it cannot recover a configured destination when the reference has no calendar ID. Google updates then receive an undefined calendarId; the equivalent delete fallback also switches to primary instead of the configured secondary calendar. Restore a usable destination fallback for references without externalCalendarId.

Co-host destinations are discarded when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination, because evt.destinationCalendar is null and the optional push does nothing. A collective booking with connected co-host calendars therefore creates none of their calendar events despite collecting their destinations. Initialize the array before appending teamDestinationCalendars.

The recurring-series branch ignores the current reference's resolved credential and still deletes only each booking's first calendar reference using the organizer's credentials. With the newly supported collective references, cancelling all remaining occurrences leaves co-host calendar events intact and repeats organizer deletions for every outer reference. For each occurrence, match its reference to the current credential and delete it through that credential.

Organization creation no longer stores slug when team billing is disabled, while requestedSlug is also omitted in that mode. createTeams rejects organizations missing both values and publish rejects a missing requestedSlug, so non-billing organization onboarding cannot proceed. Restore the previous non-billing slug assignment.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.texto: totalPages overcounts by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit. With 50 members and a limit of 50, Next remains enabled and navigates to offset 50, displaying an empty second page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) while preserving the zero-members guard.

The members endpoint now limits non-automatic groups to 50 users, but the public group-members route and template provide no pagination or load-more mechanism. Non-automatic groups with more than 50 members therefore lose access to all members after the first 50 in the public UI, whereas previously all were returned. Add public pagination alongside this response change.

Removing membership with group.users.delete leaves the removed user's primary_group_id pointing to this group. The previous usernames replacement path cleared that reference in Group#destroy_deletions, and PostSerializer still uses primary_group_id to display the user's primary group, so removed members continue displaying the former group. Clear primary_group_id for the removed user when it equals this group's ID as part of the removal.

fixing-re-authentication-with-passkeys-k.texto: PasswordForm.configuredFor now accepts passkey-only users even when the selected login theme cannot render passkey authentication on the password page. The legacy keycloak theme inherits base/login-password.ftl, which does not import or invoke conditionalUIData, so a passkey-only user reaching this execution is presented with only an unusable password field instead of a way to authenticate. Add the passkey macro to base/login-password.ftl as well as the keycloak.v2 override so the newly accepted credential can be used by both bundled themes.

frontend-asset-optimization-grafana-code.texto: The exclusive-lock path does not recheck the cache after acquiring the lock, so concurrent production requests that initially observe nil each reload the manifest sequentially even after the first request has populated the cache. A cold-start burst through index rendering or frontend-settings hashing therefore performs one serialized file read and JSON decode per waiting request instead of one initialization, delaying the queued responses. Recheck entryPointAssetsCache under the write lock and return it when cfg.Env != setting.Dev and it is non-nil before loading the manifest.

github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.texto: OAuth state uses pipeline.signature, which is a deterministic hash of pipeline view class names rather than a session-bound nonce. An attacker can initiate authorization for their own GitHub account and send the resulting callback URL to another user with an active installation pipeline; the shared state passes validation and binds the attacker's GitHub identity in the victim's pipeline. Generate a cryptographically random state, store it in pipeline state, and compare the callback against that stored value, as the existing OAuth2 views do.

Installer verification is performed only when an Integration row already exists, while the Integration.DoesNotExist branch above advances directly to pipeline completion. If the installation webhook is delayed or absent, supplying another installation ID lets an authenticated GitHub user create and link that installation without ever matching its installer; finish_pipeline only fetches installation details and ensures the integration exists. Fail closed when trusted installer metadata is unavailable instead of advancing past verification.

The new comparison indexes integration.metadata['sender']['login'] without checking whether sender exists. build_integration only stores sender when supplied in state, so integrations created by the normal pipeline before their webhook arrives can lack this metadata; attempting to reconnect such an unlinked integration now raises KeyError instead of displaying the installation error. Guard the metadata lookup and return the verification error when trusted sender information is unavailable.

implement-access-token-context-encoding-.texto: The new token-context encoding emits an unknown grant for UMA RPTs because their issuance path never sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE on the client session context. PermissionGrantType delegates issuance to AuthorizationTokenService, which creates a fresh context at lines 329-353 and calls generateAccessToken at lines 357-358 without passing through OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, so these tokens receive na instead of the registered pg shortcut. Set the UMA grant attribute on that context before generating the RPT.

The access-token ID matcher checks the wrong character range and reverses the grant comparison. Grant shortcuts occupy substring(4, 6), but substring(3, 5) combined with rejection on equality allows IDs with incorrect grants to pass the authorization-code, refresh, device and CIBA assertions. Validate the prefix length and reject when !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut).

notification-rule-processing-engine-graf.texto: Passing only promRule removes the Delete action from every Grafana rule in the new list. AlertRuleMenu still renders Delete only when `canDelete && rulerRule`, so the newly computed Prometheus delete ability cannot expose the action even for users with delete permission. Adapt the menu's delete callback and rendering to use the already available rule identifier without requiring a ruler DTO.

Passing only promRule removes the Pause/Resume action from Grafana rules in the new list. AlertRuleMenu still requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` before rendering MenuItemPauseRule, so a positive Prometheus pause ability never renders a control. Adapt the pause component and menu to accept the Prometheus rule or fetch the required ruler data on demand.

The Prometheus ability path enables Silence notifications without adapting the drawer rendering to Prometheus-only rules. Clicking the action sets showSilenceDrawer, but the drawer below is still guarded by `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`; GrafanaRuleListItem supplies no rule, so clicking Silence does nothing. Load the ruler rule on demand or adapt the drawer to the Prometheus rule before enabling this action.

Delegating combined-rule abilities to useAllRulerRuleAbilities drops the federated-group immutability check. A combined rule with group.source_tenants previously had Update and Delete marked unsupported, but the delegate hardcodes isFederated to false and now exposes editing for those rules when external-write permission is present. Preserve the combined group's isFederatedRuleGroup result when calculating its mutation abilities.

The new ModifyExport ability excludes Grafana recording rules by using isAlertingRule as its support flag. Recording rules rendered by GrafanaRuleListItem now lose the Export menu action, although the previous ruler ability supported all Grafana-managed rules and GrafanaModifyExport and its payload builder support recording rules. Use the Grafana rule type guard rather than the alerting-only guard for ModifyExport.

oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.texto: The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response instead of preserving the response contract required by the caller. Google reads res.data, Zoho CRM and Bigin read response.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken/expiresIn directly, so these integrations fail to refresh when syncing is enabled. Decode the endpoint response and adapt it to each caller's expected format, or normalize both branches and update all callers.

Google persists the entire safeParse result returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse rather than its data property. After a successful refresh the stored key becomes {success:true,data:{...}} instead of the credential object, so the next service construction fails googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key), including when credential sharing is disabled. Persist the successful result's data property.

Computed keys using Zod schema objects' toString() do not define dynamic properties, and this z.object strips actual expiry fields such as expires_in and expiry_date. With syncing enabled, Zoom subsequently computes expiry_date from missing newTokens.expires_in, producing NaN, while Office365 loses its refreshed expiry. Define the supported expiry properties explicitly and preserve required provider fields with passthrough or a suitable catchall.

Bigin passes credentialId into refreshOAuthTokens' userId argument. The sync endpoint consequently receives the credential row ID as calcomUserId rather than the owning user's ID, causing token lookup failures or fetching a different user's credentials when IDs overlap. Thread credential.userId from biginAuth into refreshAccessToken and pass that value.

The webhook indexes appStoreMetadata using the database app slug, but that map is keyed by integration directory names. For example, Google credentials use appId 'google-calendar' while apps.metadata.generated.ts exposes the metadata under 'googlecalendar', so a valid Google sync request returns 404. Resolve the metadata by its slug value instead of assuming the map key equals the database slug.

The new credential update references prisma without importing or defining it in this module; searching this file finds only this use. This introduces a TypeScript unresolved-name error and a ReferenceError when Salesforce client initialization reaches the update. Import prisma from @calcom/prisma.

Salesforce getClient now unconditionally refreshes the OAuth token on every service construction, even when the stored access token is still valid. Every instance adds a Salesforce network round trip and database write before any CRM operation, replacing the previous connection initialization that could reuse the token. Refresh only when necessary or retain jsforce's on-demand refresh behavior.

The parser replaces an omitted refresh token with the literal string "refresh_token", including when credential sharing is disabled. Office365 explicitly accepts responses without refresh_token and merges the parsed data into its existing credentials, so this overwrites the valid stored refresh token and makes subsequent token refreshes fail. Leave an omitted refresh_token absent so the caller's existing credential merge preserves the real token.

optimize-header-layout-performance-with-.texto: Making .contents a flex container leaves the header-extra-info component's outer Ember div with the default min-width:auto, while the overflow:hidden rule is on its inner .extra-info-wrapper. For a long, non-wrapping topic title, that outer flex item cannot shrink enough to preserve the existing title ellipsis and keep the navigation panel within the header. Apply min-width:0 to the actual component flex item, or move the wrapper class and its overflow constraint onto the component element.

The new flex layout makes .small-action-desc a content-sized flex item without allowing it to grow, although its edit/delete buttons still rely on float:right. For short action descriptions, those controls now sit beside the description instead of at the right edge of the action row. Give .small-action-desc flex:1 so its right-floated controls retain their available row width.

replays-self-serve-bulk-delete-system-se.texto: The feature-enabled table branch passes empty columns, rows, and metadata instead of the fetched result. Organizations with use-table-widget-visualization enabled therefore see empty dashboard tables even when the query returns data. Pass result.data and result.meta to the visualization and derive columns from the configured fields.

The new attribute-key query key omits organization identity although its query function requests an organization-specific endpoint. Switching organizations with identical project selections such as all projects and the same date range reuses the previous organization's cached attributes and can share an in-flight response. Include organization.slug in the query key.

Error messages are read from a top-level message field, but stored events expose their message through logentry.formatted or logentry.message as implemented by Event.message. Replay summaries consequently lose the message text of ordinary stored error/log events. Extract the logentry fields using the same fallback as Event.message.

Zipping error_ids with events.values() assumes nodestore.get_multi preserves request order, but that implementation merges uncached results with cached results and can reorder them. With a partially cached batch, error details receive another event's ID. Iterate paired error_ids and node_ids and look up each event by node ID instead.

The custom body renderer is accepted only when its return value is truthy, despite the API specifying that only undefined triggers fallback. Valid React results such as 0, an empty string, or null are replaced by the default field renderer, producing incorrect content or defeating deliberate cell suppression. Check cell !== undefined, and apply the same contract to the header renderer.

The new HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES exclusion runs only when a nonempty search query is present, because the empty-search branch returns sorted attributes before reaching this filter. Consequently is_segment, project_id, and received remain visible in the default attributes view but disappear when searched for. Apply the hidden-attribute exclusion before the empty-search early return, then apply the text-search predicate separately.

sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.texto: The new retry update inside the catch block throws when the reminder has been deleted since the initial findMany. Booking cancellation deletes these rows through deleteScheduledSMSReminder; if cancellation overlaps scheduling, the scheduling update fails and this second update fails again, escaping the catch and aborting scheduling for every remaining reminder in the batch. Use updateMany with the reminder ID for the failure counter so a concurrently deleted row is a no-op, or handle the record-not-found error within this cleanup path.

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.texto: The new isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard skips killing every production worker because multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process creates SpawnProcess instances, which are sibling subclasses of BaseProcess rather than subclasses of multiprocessing.Process. When a worker hangs, _ensure_processes_alive starts a replacement and drops the reference to the still-running worker, allowing both to flush the same shards if the old worker resumes and accumulating orphan workers across restarts. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or self.mp_context.Process before killing the worker.

The new loop calls get_memory_info once per flusher buffer even though each call retrieves memory information for the entire Redis cluster, not just that buffer's assigned shards. With P flusher processes and N Redis nodes, every submit with memory backpressure enabled now performs P full-cluster INFO scans instead of one, multiplying synchronous Redis work on the main consumer thread without changing the resulting memory ratio. Query cluster memory once using any one buffer rather than repeating it for every process.

unified-storage-performance-optimization.texto: Locking only cache publication allows concurrent cache misses for the same NamespacedResource to build and publish different indexes. Search and the watch-event handler both call getOrCreateIndex, so one build can publish an index and receive live updates before another in-flight build overwrites it with an older snapshot, losing those updates from search results. Coordinate builds per key and recheck the cache inside that coordination while retaining parallel builds for different keys.

The new TotalDocs call iterates bleveBackend.cache without a read lock after the watch-event consumer has already started. An event for a previously unindexed namespace/resource can concurrently publish an index through BuildIndex, causing a map iteration/write data race and potentially a fatal concurrent-map panic during initialization. Protect TotalDocs cache iteration with cacheMu.RLock/RUnlock.
